key_insight: The paper suggests that independently trained image generators share surprisingly compatible latent representations and denoising behavior, making it possible to build a common interface across different model families. In simple terms, very different generators may speak a similar internal "latent language."
problem_solved: Modern image generators such as diffusion and flow models use heterogeneous architectures and representations, which makes cross-model comparison, alignment, and reuse difficult. This work addresses the lack of a shared latent interface for unifying these diverse generators.
method: Analyze latent-space compatibility across independently trained image generators.
Identify shared structure in their denoising dynamics and latent representations.
Propose a shared latent interface that can connect heterogeneous generators through a common internal representation.
impact: For practitioners, this could simplify model interoperability, transfer, and comparison across different generator architectures. It may also enable more flexible toolchains for editing, benchmarking, and composing image generation systems.
visual_elements: Side-by-side diagram of different image generators converging into one shared latent space

Icon set comparing heterogeneous architectures connected by a common interface
paper_title: InstantFusion: A Shared Latent Interface for Heterogeneous Image Generators
paper_authors: Xuanlang Dai, Jiazi Bu, Yujie Zhou, Yuhong Liu, Beichen Zhang
